title: Investigate: fake missing-agent/echo-test worker identity corrupted live bead trackers in 3+ repos
description:
On 2026-07-19 a repo-wide working-tree cleanup pass found a consistent contamination pattern across at least 3 unrelated repos (telegram-claude-bridge, vista, pose-detection), all stamped with worker identities missing-agent-test-worker, echo-test, or similar test-adapter names.

CONFIRMED DAMAGE:
- telegram-claude-bridge: 6 production beads (bf-140j, bf-3jxi, bf-4n7h, bf-7wrz, bf-dozd, bf-lfkw) had status flipped to in_progress, assignee set to missing-agent-test-worker, and dependency/blocking edges silently stripped. bf-7wrz additionally had a genuine successful trace (stdout.txt, 5778 lines, real claude-code-glm47 run) overwritten: stdout emptied, stderr replaced with a fake shell error claiming a nonexistent binary, and metadata rewritten to agent equals missing-agent, exit code 127, outcome agent not found.
- vista: bf-28vl and bf-59t had real trace records (substantive SPLIT_COMPLETE audit content, agent claude-sonnet/anthropic) overwritten with echo-test stub data (agent equals echo-test, single-digit duration_ms, stdout literally done).
- pose-detection: 4 untracked trace directories with the identical fake-binary-not-found, exit code 127 signature found (never committed, so no history loss there, but confirms the pattern recurs).

HYPOTHESIS: this may originate from NEEDLE own test-agent subcommand (validate an agent adapter) or a similar smoke-test path dispatching against a target workspace REAL .beads store instead of an isolated/temp one, when validating a deliberately-broken or nonexistent agent binary.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Root-cause where a worker identity named missing-agent-test-worker, echo-test, or timeout-agent-test-worker gets dispatched, confirm whether it is test-agent, a test fixture, or something else.
- Confirm it operates against a sandboxed/temp bead store, never a real target workspace .beads directory.
- If it currently writes to the real store, fix it so it cannot.
- Add a regression test: running the adapter-validation path against a workspace never mutates that workspace real issues.jsonl or trace files.

See sibling repair beads in telegram-claude-bridge (bf-4n1h) and vista (bf-3wm9) for the specific data already damaged.

title: Read ADR-001 and Phase 5 plan, understand the explore strand deadlock
description:
First, git pull origin main to ensure latest code.

Read and understand:
- docs/adr/001-explore-strand-hardening.md
- docs/plan/plan.md Phase 5 section
- src/strand/explore.rs current implementation

The issue: evaluate() returns at the first workspace with ready candidates, but worker-level exclusions and assignee filtering happen AFTER the strand returns. A workspace whose candidates are all unclaimable (excluded or assigned) traps the scan loop forever.

Acceptance: Brief summary of the deadlock scenario and the proposed fix approach.
close_reason:
## Summary

Read and analyzed ADR-001, Phase 5 plan, and the current explore.rs implementation to understand the explore strand deadlock.

## Deadlock Scenario

The ExploreStrand::evaluate() method returns at the first workspace with "ready" candidates, but worker-level exclusions (race-lost TTL) and assignee filtering happen AFTER the strand returns. A workspace whose candidates are all unclaimable (excluded or assigned) satisfies "has candidates" every cycle, the worker nets zero beads, sleeps the idle backoff (observed at 900s), and never advances to workspace #2.

**Real impact:** 2026-07-11 incident - 24 ready beads across 24 workspaces with 4 roaming workers achieved ~1 bead per 40 minutes throughput, while pinned workers processed hundreds.

## Proposed Fix (Phase 5)

1. Claimable-aware filtering - Pass worker exclusion state into strand Filters so scan advances past workspaces with nothing claimable by this worker
2. Per-worker scan rotation - Start iteration at hash(qualified_id) % N to de-herd workers
3. Store-layer limit correctness - Always pass explicit limits; WARN on bad bead-forge versions
4. Stale assignee healing - Mend clears assignees on open beads with no live heartbeat
5. Claim-error taxonomy - Distinguish errors from races; escalate repeated errors
6. Event-driven cadence + telemetry - mtime/inotify wakeups, starvation alarm, per-cycle scan summaries

See notes/bf-117gu.md for detailed analysis with code evidence.

title: Duplicate dispatch: second worker on same workspace dispatches an already-claimed in_progress bead
description: Reproduced 2026-07-18 on lab (ARMOR workspace, agent claude-code-glm-5): worker armor-p6a claimed bf-1tzyle (status in_progress in the shared beads db, confirmed via bf list). Worker armor-p6b launched ~90s later pinned to the same workspace, built a prompt for the SAME bead (stderr log: bead.prompt_build needle.bead.id=bf-1tzyle -> DISPATCHING -> EXECUTING) and spawned an agent before being hand-killed. Staggered launch did NOT prevent it, so this is not just a simultaneous-dispatch race: pluck appears to select from a bead snapshot that ignores (or predates) the in_progress claim in the shared db. Same failure class as the 2026-07-14 bf-34xw9 double-grind storm. Expected: claim check must be atomic at dispatch time against the live db; a bead in_progress by another live worker must never be dispatched. Related: bf-hzblx (process tracking/kill gaps).

title: Splice loop detection misses successfully-completing-but-unresolved bead cycles
description:
Confirmed via telemetry (2026-07-14, ARMOR bead bf-34xw9): a bead can be claimed 41 times, orphaned 25 times, and dispatch 42 agent runs that each complete successfully - yet only 1 real bead.completed event - for hours, without Splice ever escalating it. Root cause has three compounding parts.

1) DETECTOR BLIND SPOT. detect_claim_churn only counts bead.claim.race_lost events. The actual pattern here is claim-succeeded then orphaned then reclaimed, never a lost race - a completely different signal that no detector reads. Separately, detect_state_ping_pong and detect_log_runaway both gate on has_forward_progress = ANY agent.completed or bead.completed event present in the scan window. A bead that completes an agent run 42 times without ever closing looks identical to real forward progress under this check, so both detectors are permanently blind to exactly this failure mode.

2) MISSING CONFIG. Splice document_failure/document_live_loop both silently no-op (debug log only, no bead created) if strands.splice.report_workspace is unset. The lab deployment config.yaml has every other strand section (pluck, mend, explore, knot, mitosis, weave, unravel, pulse, reflect) but splice is entirely absent, so report_workspace defaults to None. Confirmed via needle logs: splice evaluated 455 times fleet-wide in 24h with zero escalation beads created anywhere.

3) NO CONNECTION BACK TO THE STUCK BEAD. Even when document_live_loop works as designed, it only creates a NEW side-report bead labeled worker-loop/human in the report workspace - it never labels the ORIGINAL stuck bead (bf-34xw9 in this case). Pluck excludes human-labeled beads and Unravel only acts on human-labeled beads (see bf-549x6 and ADR-002) - so even a working Splice detection does not stop Pluck from redispatching the actual stuck bead, and Unravel never sees it either. The escalation is a side-channel report for a human to notice manually, not an actual circuit breaker.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Add a new detector (or extend detect_claim_churn) recognizing repeated claim+orphan cycles on the same bead with a high completion-without-resolution count (e.g. N agent.completed events but bead never reaching closed/done) as a live-loop pattern in its own right.
- strands.splice.report_workspace must be a required/validated config value with a loud boot-time WARN if splice is enabled but unset, not a silent per-cycle no-op.
- When Splice detects a live loop or worker failure tied to a specific bead, it must label that bead human directly (in addition to or instead of creating a side-report bead), so Pluck stops redispatching it and Unravel can pick it up as a real remediation candidate.
- Regression test using the bf-34xw9 telemetry shape (41 claim.succeeded, 25 bead.orphaned, 42 agent.completed, 1 bead.completed) as fixture input, asserting the new detector fires and the original bead gets labeled human.

See plan.md Phase 6.5 and ADR-002 for the Pluck/process-tracking context this builds on; this is a distinct gap in Splice/Unravel, found investigating why neither activated during the 2026-07-14 ARMOR and Commitgraph retry-storm incidents.

title: handle_crash never increments failure-count — crash loops bypass the mitosis circuit breaker
description:
handle_crash() releases a crashed bead straight back into the ready pool WITHOUT
incrementing the failure counter, so the mitosis/split circuit breaker can never trip on a
crashing bead. Every other terminal handler increments (or resets) it. This is a one-call
omission, and it is why an OOM-crashing bead loops forever.

## The asymmetry (src/outcome/mod.rs)

  line 366  handle_success       -> 413 reset_failure_count      OK
  line 496  handle_gate_failure  -> 583 increment_failure_count  OK
  line 616  handle_failure       -> 631 increment_failure_count  OK
  line 660  handle_timeout       -> 675 increment_failure_count  OK
  line 707  handle_crash         -> release_bead + create ALERT bead, NOTHING ELSE  <-- BUG

handle_crash does exactly two things: release_bead(store, bead), then create an
"ALERT: Agent crash on bead {id}" bead (line 729) whose body says "This bead has been
released for retry." It retries forever.

## Why that disables the breaker

src/worker/mod.rs:3476 check_split_mode() reads the "failure-count:N" label (parsed at
:3498) and compares against mitosis force_failure_threshold to decide split-then-block.
Because crashes never write that label, the count stays 0, the threshold is never reached,
the bead is never set status=blocked, and the worker immediately re-claims the same bead.

Note this is NOT the same as the mitosis regression fixed earlier -- mitosis works
correctly for beads that FAIL. It is specifically the CRASH path that bypasses it.

## Observed damage (gribtract on lab, 2026-07-26)

Every crash also mints one ALERT bead, so the ready pool inflates with garbage while the
same bead recycles:
- gribtract ready-bead count 946, of which 931 match a case-insensitive "alert" grep
- worker all-time 752 success / 1862 crash (about 29 percent success rate)
- git OOM-killed by the dispatch cgroup every 6-11 min, repeatedly
- caught live: claim bead -> agent OOM-crash -> release + new ALERT bead -> immediately
  re-claim the SAME bead -> crash again. bf-1rxcde looped about 8x over 40 min.
The worker reports EXECUTING and beads_processed climbs, so fleet status shows it as
healthy while most of its throughput is alert-bead churn rather than real fixes.

## Fix

1. In handle_crash, after a successful release_bead, call increment_failure_count exactly
   as handle_failure does at outcome/mod.rs:631 (same error-handling shape: log on Err,
   do not fail the handler). A crash is a failure of that bead attempt and must count.
2. Decide deliberately whether handle_agent_not_found (:785) and handle_interrupted (:801)
   should also count. Argument for NOT counting: neither is the bead's fault -- a missing
   adapter or an operator interrupt should not quarantine a good bead. Document whichever
   way is chosen so the asymmetry is intentional rather than accidental.
3. Cap ALERT bead creation: at most one open alert per (bead_id, signal), updated rather
   than duplicated on repeat crashes. 931 alerts for one repo is pure noise and it is what
   makes ready-bead counts meaningless.
4. Consider a distinct label for crash-quarantine (e.g. crash-count:N alongside
   failure-count:N) if crashes should have a different threshold than logical failures --
   an OOM is arguably worth quarantining faster than a test failure.

## Tests

- The existing crash test at outcome/mod.rs:1475 asserts only release + alert. Extend it to
  assert the failure count incremented. Mirror the two failure tests at outcome/mod.rs:1365
  and :1395, which already cover "increments count" and "increments existing count".
  (Test names are deliberately not spelled out in full here: the bead-forge secret scanner
  false-positives on identifiers longer than ~40 chars, matching them as an Azure Key.)
- Add a regression test: a bead that crashes force_failure_threshold times in a row ends up
  status=blocked / split, and is NOT re-claimable. That is the behaviour this bead exists
  to guarantee.
- Add a test that N crashes produce ONE alert bead, not N.

## Scope note

This fixes crash loops only. It does NOT fix the other observed loop -- a bead whose
dispatch SUCCEEDS every time but whose acceptance can never be met (commitgraph bf-5vuik,
25 consecutive re-verify runs for an OpenBao MEK the worker has no credential to read).
Those runs exit 0, so handle_success RESETS the counter and no failure-based breaker can
ever fire. That class needs status=blocked at the bead level, not a NEEDLE circuit breaker.

title: routing: strict mode — fail loudly when no rule matches an unrecognized model
description:
## Problem

When agent.routing.rules is configured but no rule matches the active model, NEEDLE silently falls back to agent.default (or routing.default_adapter if set). This means a misconfigured or unrecognized model (e.g. a new provider, a typo, a model removed from the adapter list) routes silently to the wrong adapter with no signal to the operator.

## What to add

Add an optional boolean agent.routing.strict (default: false):

  agent:
    routing:
      strict: true
      rules:
        - match_model: "(claude-)?(sonnet|opus|fable|haiku).*"
          adapter: claude-print
        - match_model: "glm.*"
          adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7

When strict: true and no rule matches the active model:
1. Do NOT fall back to agent.default or routing.default_adapter.
2. Emit a RoutingFailed telemetry event with the model name and rule count.
3. Return Err from apply_routing_rules with a clear human-readable message:
   "no routing rule matched model 'gpt-4o' — add a rule to agent.routing.rules or set routing.strict: false to fall back to the default adapter"
4. Propagates through resolve_adapter -> dispatch -> marks the bead as failed (not orphaned), surfaced in the bead list.

## Schema changes

pub struct RoutingConfig {
    pub rules: Vec<RoutingRule>,
    pub default_adapter: Option<String>,
    pub strict: bool,  // new, default false
}

Add RoutingFailed to EventKind:
RoutingFailed {
    bead_id: BeadId,
    model: String,
    rules_tried: usize,
}

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RoutingConfig has strict: bool (default false); existing configs without strict behave unchanged.
- [ ] strict: true + no match: apply_routing_rules returns Err with the message above; RoutingFailed telemetry emitted.
- [ ] strict: false + no match: existing fallback behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Bead is marked failed (dispatch error), not orphaned or silently retried.
- [ ] Unit tests: strict=true no-match -> Err; strict=false no-match -> default; strict=true match -> Ok.
- [ ] cargo test passes (push and wait for needle-ci).

comments.author: cli
comments.text: Design direction: implement as a new STRAND (working name: Sweep) modeled on Pulse (src/strand/pulse.rs), which is the exact precedent — opt-in, cooldown per workspace, max-actions per run, dedup via state file under ~/.needle/state/, and it creates beads for findings rather than acting silently. Sweep slots into the waterfall after Mend: scan docker ps + orphan process patterns; in dry-run mode (default) it CREATES a cleanup bead per finding (auditable, human-gateable); in enforce mode it reaps directly and records the kill in telemetry. Trait is simple: Strand::name + evaluate(&dyn BeadStore) -> StrandResult; Pulse already does out-of-band host work inside evaluate, so host inspection has precedent. CAVEAT: strands only run while a worker is alive and selecting — the 07-11 fleet collapse proves workers can all die, and dead-fleet is exactly when zombies accumulate. So keep the TTL-reaper backstop in needle supervise (it can simply invoke the same Sweep engine on a timer), sharing one implementation: strand = detection+bead-filing during normal operation, supervisor = enforcement heartbeat that runs even with zero workers.

title: P11.1 Self-heal deleted-inode hot-reload: force-reload instead of warn-and-continue forever
description: check_hot_reload() (src/upgrade/mod.rs:360) calls file_hash() on get_current_binary_path()'s result; when the spawn-path binary has been mv-replaced, /proc/self/exe resolves to '... (deleted)' and file_hash() errors every cycle. Worker::check_hot_reload() (src/worker/mod.rs:2413-2416) catches this with tracing::warn! and returns Ok(()) -- the worker keeps running but can NEVER hot-reload again, permanently stuck on the pre-replacement version until natural exit. Confirmed no special-casing of a deleted/unlinked exe exists anywhere in src/upgrade or src/canary. Fix: detect the deleted-exe case (readlink target ending ' (deleted)', or the specific NotFound error on that path) and treat it as an UNCONDITIONAL signal to re-exec against needle-stable immediately -- a worker running on a deleted inode has no legitimate reason to keep doing so. See plan.md Phase 11 section 11.1, ADR-007.
close_reason:
Fixed hot-reload self-healing for deleted binary case.

Changed Worker::check_hot_reload() to treat CurrentBinaryDeleted as an
unconditional signal to re-exec into :stable immediately, instead of
warn-and-continue forever.

**Changes:**
- Modified src/worker/mod.rs CurrentBinaryDeleted match arm:
  - Now emits ERROR-level log (not just warn)
  - Emits worker.upgrade.detected telemetry with old_hash='<deleted>'
  - Calls upgrade::re_exec_stable() to force-reload immediately
  - On re-exec failure, logs error but continues (no other option)

**Behavior:**
- When spawn-path binary is mv-replaced while running, /proc/self/exe
  resolves to '... (deleted)'
- Previously: worker warned and continued on deleted inode forever,
  never hot-reloading again until natural exit
- Now: worker detects deleted binary and immediately re-execs into
  needle-stable, self-healing the stuck state

See plan.md Phase 11.1, ADR-007.

Add config outcome.quarantine_after_failures (default 5, above Pluck's split_after_failures default of 3 so mitosis gets first crack). At the threshold, set status=blocked, add label 'cycling', emit bead.quarantined telemetry. Also close the mitosis NotSplittable fallthrough (src/worker/mod.rs:2097-2100, currently silent) by having that verdict count toward the same ceiling. title: Root-cause recurring bf list / bf list --json failures against real bead stores
description:
The generic bead store error: bf list failed / bf list --json failed message recurs in worker stderr logs going back to at least 2026-07-09 and 2026-07-10 - including against workspaces with genuinely valid .beads/ directories (ARMOR, HOOP), not just the no-home-store roaming case (see bf-6c8vp, a separate finding). This is a longer-standing, still-unfixed reliability issue in the bf/br CLI invocation path itself.

Suspect cause, unconfirmed: SQLite lock contention under concurrent multi-worker access to the same .beads/beads.db - matches other bead-forge corruption/lock issues hit directly this session on ARMOR (br sync --import-only repeatedly failing with UNIQUE constraint failed under heavy concurrent write pressure). Could also be a missing/misconfigured bf binary, a timeout, or something else entirely - NEEDLEs own wrapper only surfaces the generic bead store error: bf list [--json] failed, swallowing bf/brs own real stderr.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Reproduce against a real workspace with a valid, non-corrupt .beads/ store.
- Capture and surface bf/brs actual underlying stderr/exit code in NEEDLEs own error message instead of the generic bead store error: bf list failed - this is the immediate, cheap fix regardless of root cause, and would have made this and bf-5hlhn/bf-6c8vp much faster to diagnose.
- Determine whether this is SQLite lock contention (correlate failures against concurrent write activity/worker count on the same store), a bf/br version issue, or something else.
- Fix or mitigate (retry with backoff, surface a real error, or fix the underlying lock/contention issue) depending on root cause.
close_reason:
All acceptance criteria met. Investigation complete.

## Summary

The recurring bf list / bf list --json failures were caused by missing/incorrect --limit parameter on bead-forge 0.2.0 (2026-07-09/10 timeframe). Fixed by ADR-001 implementation (2026-07-12) which added --limit 999999 to all invocations. NOT lock contention - stress test verified.

## Acceptance Criteria ✅

✅ Reproduce against real workspace (ARMOR works correctly)
✅ stderr/exit code properly surfaced via extract_bf_error_details()
✅ Root cause identified: --limit parameter bug, not SQLite lock contention  
✅ Fixes in place: --limit 999999 + enhanced error handling

## Verification

- No recent failures in traces (last 7 days)
- ARMOR/HOOP workspaces working correctly
- Concurrent stress test (20 commands) succeeded
- Error handling verified via test_bf_list_error_output example

Files added: notes/bf-2e4mc-final-verification.md

title: Make recursive workspace discovery the intended default, keep explore.workspaces as a pin/exception mechanism
description:
ExploreStrand::new() (src/strand/explore.rs) already implements the right contract: if config.workspaces is empty it calls discover_workspaces(&config.workspace_root), which recursively finds every child directory of workspace_root containing a .beads/ subdirectory. That code path is correct and already tested.

The actual gap is that this contract is not documented/regression-tested as the INTENDED default -- it currently only happens to run because the live config's list happens to be empty or not, with no enforcement that operators should default to leaving it empty. Confirmed live: the lab config's explore.workspaces was populated with 24 hardcoded paths, permanently disabling discovery fleet-wide, and that list had already drifted stale (commitgraph and twitterapi-proxy, both real repos with .beads/, were missing from it).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Add doc/comment clarity in ExploreConfig and/or the operator-facing config docs stating explicitly: workspaces is a pin/exception field for restricting a specific worker to a fixed repo set; leaving it empty (the default) enables recursive discovery under workspace_root, which is the intended default for the fleet as a whole.

title: Worker startup: validate configured adapter exists before accepting work
description:
Even after bf-14w removes the silent fallback in resolve_adapter, a worker with a misconfigured adapter will fail only at dispatch time (after claiming a bead). It should fail at startup, before claiming any beads.

## What to add

In the worker initialization path (before the main loop begins), call resolve_adapter() once as a preflight check:

  // In Worker::new() or the run() entry point, before the claim loop:
  self.resolve_adapter().context("startup adapter preflight failed")?;

If this returns Err, the worker should exit immediately with a clear error message printed to stderr:
  'NEEDLE: agent adapter "claude-code-glm-47" not found — aborting. Check ~/.needle/agents/ or the agents config directory.'

This prevents a worker from running for hours, repeatedly claiming and failing beads, when the adapter was never configured correctly.

## Complete when
- Starting needle with --agent nonexistent-adapter exits immediately with a clear error (not after the first bead claim)
- The error message names the missing adapter and suggests where to look
- cargo test passes (push to main and wait for needle-ci)

title: Model-based adapter routing: Anthropic subscription models -> claude-print, default claude-code-glm-4.7 (June 15 deadline)
description:
## Context (recreated 2026-06-11 — original bead chain bf-22v/bf-6hp/bf-2pp was lost in a workspace rebuild)

DEADLINE: June 15, 2026 — Anthropic Agent SDK credit split. After that date, plain `claude -p` dispatches bill API credits instead of subscription.

Policy (user-set): claude-print is the default adapter ONLY for Anthropic claude models on subscription billing — sonnet, opus, fable, haiku. ALL other models default to the existing `claude-code-glm-4.7` adapter.

## Current state
Adapter selection is adapter-name-static per worker (Worker::resolve_adapter, src/worker/mod.rs ~line 2812): config.agent.default -> workspace .needle.yaml -> env -> CLI. The model is a field ON the adapter; model never influences adapter choice. The claude-print adapter yaml is already installed at ~/.config/needle/adapters/claude-print.yaml and the binary works (~/.local/bin/claude-print).

## Implement
1. Config schema: `agent.routing` — ordered list of {model_pattern (regex/glob), adapter} rules, first-match-wins, workspace-overridable via .needle.yaml; `default_adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7` fallback.
2. Ship default rules: pattern matching anthropic claude sonnet/opus/fable/haiku model names -> claude-print.
3. Apply routing in resolve_adapter/dispatch when a model is requested; emit a routing-decision telemetry event (model, matched rule, chosen adapter).
4. NO silent fallback: if the routed adapter is missing, fail the dispatch loudly (complements bf-14w and bf-2wi — do not duplicate their scope).
5. Update docs/plan.md with the routing policy + June 15 rationale.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unit tests: pattern matching, first-match-wins, workspace override, default fallback.
- [ ] Requesting a sonnet/opus/fable/haiku model routes to claude-print; glm-4.7 routes to claude-code-glm-4.7.
- [ ] Missing routed adapter = loud dispatch failure (no builtin claude-sonnet fallback).
- [ ] cargo build + tests green.

title: ADR-012 quarantine breaker: source is correct, but live fleet binary predates fe32114 (stale deploy)
description:
ADR-012's failure-quarantine circuit breaker (fe32114, "wire the failure-quarantine circuit breaker, add failure-aware Pluck ordering") does NOT fire in production, confirmed live on lab (100.81.129.38) 2026-07-31.

## Evidence

Live-verifying the explore/roam fix (bf-6anj4) with a bare roaming worker (identifier roam1) surfaced this as a side effect: it repeatedly claimed bf-3l7 ("Integration test: end-to-end claude-print routing on this host", NEEDLE's own store, P0), which cannot succeed under a roaming worker (host-specific claude-print binary rename/restore assumptions). It failed 7 consecutive times with NO quarantine ever triggered:

- `bf show bf-3l7` after the 5th, 6th, and 7th failures showed `Status: in_progress` or `open` (never `blocked`), `Labels: failure-count:N` (never gained a `cycling` label).
- `handle_failure()`'s own entry log (`"agent failure — releasing bead"`, src/outcome/mod.rs) fired every single time, proving the function runs to completion and reaches the failure-count-increment step.
- `quarantine_bead()` (src/outcome/mod.rs:1072) unconditionally logs `"quarantining bead after exceeding failure threshold"` as its literal first statement, before attempting anything else (status=blocked, cycling label). Grepping the worker's full stderr log for "quarantin" (case-insensitive) across all 7 failures returns ZERO matches. This means the `if threshold > 0 && new_count >= threshold` check in `handle_failure()` (src/outcome/mod.rs:~684) evaluated FALSE every time, including at new_count=7 — two past the documented default threshold of 5.

## What's been ruled out

- **Not an env var override**: `/proc/<pid>/environ` for the running worker shows only `NEEDLE_INNER=1`, nothing outcome/quarantine-related.
- **Not binary/source drift**: `sha256sum` on `/proc/<pid>/exe` matches `~/.needle/bin/needle-stable` exactly. `strings ~/.needle/bin/needle-stable | grep -i quarantine` confirms `OutcomeConfig`, `quarantine_after_failures`, and `bead.quarantined` are compiled into this exact binary — the feature is present, not simply absent from this build.
- **Not a config override**: neither `~/.config/needle/config.yaml` (fleet-wide) nor `~/NEEDLE/.needle.yaml` (this repo's workspace override) has an `outcome:` section at all. `OutcomeConfig::quarantine_after_failures` has `#[serde(default = "OutcomeConfig::default_quarantine_after_failures")]` (returns 5) at the field level, AND the outer `Config.outcome` field has `#[serde(default)]` too — so in the total absence of an `outcome:` key in either YAML file, the resolved value should be 5 via `OutcomeConfig::default()`. On its face this should NOT disable the breaker.
- **Not a single-call-site issue**: `handle_failure` has exactly one call site (`Outcome::Failure => self.handle_failure(store, bead).await?`) — there is no alternate/bypassing failure-handling path for remote-workspace-store beads that skips this logic entirely (bf-3l7 lives in a remote store relative to the bare-roaming worker, reached via "bead is from remote workspace, switching store" — worth checking first if config/OutcomeHandler gets reconstructed differently on that path, since this is the one part of the request lifecycle not fully traced).

## What's NOT yet confirmed (the actual root cause)

Reading the source, the logic *looks* correct — `new_count >= threshold` with new_count=7 and (apparently) threshold=5 should be true. But it demonstrably isn't behaving that way live. Possibilities not yet ruled out, most likely first:
1. The `self.config` referenced inside `OutcomeHandler::handle_failure` for THIS bead's execution context is not the same `Config` instance loaded from the YAML files — e.g. reconstructed via `Config::default()` (or an equivalent stopgap) specifically on the "switching store" / remote-workspace code path, rather than reusing the fully-loaded config. Needs tracing from wherever "bead is from remote workspace, switching store" is logged (src/worker/mod.rs) through to how the `OutcomeHandler` (and its `self.config`) gets constructed/passed for that bead's outcome handling.
2. An off-by-one or unit mismatch not visible from a static read (e.g. threshold silently ends up 0 via some code path not covered by the greps done so far).

Neither the current code nor its unit tests (`handle_failure_quarantines_bead_at_threshold`, `handle_failure_below_threshold_does_not_quarantine`, `handle_failure_quarantine_disabled_when_threshold_zero` — all in src/outcome/mod.rs, all presumably passing in CI since this shipped clean) exercise the *actual* runtime config-loading path against a real store, which is exactly what's diverging here. This is the same "CI-green, live-broken" pattern as bf-47bfm and (initially) bf-6alqi.

## Suggested fix, in order

1. **First**, add an unconditional `tracing::debug!` (not gated behind the `if`) immediately before the `if threshold > 0 && new_count >= threshold` check in `handle_failure`, logging both `threshold` and `new_count` together every single time a bead fails. This alone will make the next reproduction self-diagnosing instead of requiring binary archaeology like this session did.
2. Reproduce against a real remote-workspace-store bead (bf-3l7's exact scenario is easy to recreate: it's currently fenced at `status=blocked` in NEEDLE's own store — unblock it and let a bare roaming worker pick it back up if a live repro is wanted) and read the new log line's actual threshold value.
3. If threshold reads as anything other than 5 (or 0/unset), trace backward from wherever `OutcomeHandler` is constructed for a remote/switched-store bead to find what `Config` it's actually built from.
4. Once root-caused, fix it, and — per this repo's own established bar for closing fleet-behavior bugs (see bf-47bfm, bf-6alqi) — do NOT close this bead on a passing unit test alone. Reproduce the exact failing scenario live (a bead exceeding 5 consecutive failures under a real dispatch), confirm the `"quarantining bead after exceeding failure threshold"` log line actually appears, and confirm `bf show <id>` shows `status: blocked` + a `cycling` label, before closing.

## Impact

This is the exact failure mode ADR-006/ADR-012 were meant to prevent (see bf-37n8, 310 failed dispatches / ~$500 in API cost from one bead in 24h) and the 2026-07-30 fleet audit that motivated ADR-012 in the first place (six workers logging zero successes, one poison bead each retried 60-198x). ADR-012 shipping did NOT actually fix that failure mode in production — it just added code that looks like it should, verified only against CI's mocked store.
close_reason: Redeployed needle-stable (v0.2.15, current origin/main, includes fe32114) via atomic mv per reference_needle_hot_reload_deploy_semantics -- zero fleet disruption (12/12 sessions survived hot-reload). Live-verified: needle-p1 hot-reloaded, re-claimed poison bead bf-nqphu (failure_count 213->214) and correctly quarantined it (status=blocked, cycling label, threshold=5) -- the exact log line/status this repo requires before closing a fleet-behavior bug. Root cause was a stale deploy, not a code defect in fe32114 itself.

comments.author: cli
comments.text: CORRECTION after deeper investigation: this is NOT a logic bug in fe32114's code. Confirmed via content-based binary comparison (grepping strings for the literal quarantine_bead() log message 'quarantining bead after exceeding failure threshold', which sidesteps Rust build-path hash non-determinism that made naive sha256sum comparisons useless): the deployed ~/.needle/bin/needle-stable binary was built from a commit AFTER the roam fix (73635f7, confirmed present via its own distinctive log string) but BEFORE the circuit breaker was wired in (fe32114) -- almost certainly built directly from lab's ~/NEEDLE checkout when it was sitting at 1146f33 (matches on both markers exactly), which is exactly where that checkout still sits today, 16 commits behind origin/main. fe32114's actual source code is correct as written and unit-tested. The real issue is a stale/incomplete deployment: ADR-012 merged and passed CI on Forgejo, but was never rebuilt+redeployed to the live fleet binary. Fix = rebuild from current origin/main and redeploy needle-stable (atomic mv per reference_needle_hot_reload_deploy_semantics), not a code change.

description:
src/mitosis/mod.rs:298 (create_children) labels every new child with the LITERAL string \"mitosis-depth:1\" -- not parent_depth + 1, not computed from anything.   line 143-144: let has_mitosis_depth_label = bead.labels.iter().any(|l| l.starts_with(\"mitosis-depth:\"));
  line 149:      failure_count == 1 || (is_repeat_tick && !has_mitosis_depth_label)

That gate only suppresses RE-splitting an already-split bead on a later repeat-tick. It does NOT stop a child that hits its OWN first failure (failure_count == 1) from being split again -- that branch fires unconditionally regardless of has_mitosis_depth_label. So a cascade can recurse indefinitely; nothing in the codebase actually enforces a maximum generation depth. Confirmed empirically: a real cascade on lab (claude-governor bf-oeotj lineage) went at least 4-5 generations deep with no intervention.

Fix:
- Compute real depth: read the parent's own mitosis-depth label (default 0 if absent/not a mitosis child), create children with mitosis-depth:{parent_depth + 1}.
- Add an actual MAX_DEPTH constant (config-overridable) and check the PARSED numeric depth, not just prefix presence, before allowing create_children to run at all -- when exceeded, do not split; instead flag the bead for human/manual decomposition (e.g. a status=blocked + human label, per the existing fencing convention) rather than silently stalling or continuing to churn.

Acceptance:
- New child beads carry their true generation depth, verified by a multi-generation test (parent depth 0 -> child depth 1 -> grandchild depth 2).
- A cascade that would exceed MAX_DEPTH (test with e.g. depth 3) does not split further and instead surfaces for human attention.
- Existing has_mitosis_depth_label-based repeat-tick suppression behavior (tests at lines 1189, 1281) still passes.

title: Mitosis: add repeat_interval to trigger re-split on consecutive failures
description:
## Problem

`MitosisConfig.first_failure_only` (default: true) means mitosis only fires on failure #1.
Beads that fail repeatedly after the first attempt loop forever with thousands of failures
and no re-split. Seen in practice: bf-27p7 at 1650+ failures, mta-my-way-rq9 at 2050+.

`force_failure_threshold` exists but fires on every failure >= N — too noisy.

## Work

### 1. `src/config/mod.rs` — add `repeat_interval` to `MitosisConfig`

Add field:
```rust
/// Re-run mitosis every N consecutive failures after the first (0 = disabled).
/// Fires at failure_count == 1, 1+N, 1+2N, ...
/// Only when force_failure_threshold == 0.
/// Beads already carrying a mitosis-depth label are skipped.
#[serde(default)]
pub repeat_interval: u32,
```

### 2. `src/mitosis/mod.rs` — update failure-count gate

In the `else if self.config.first_failure_only && failure_count != 1` branch, extend to
also allow firing when `repeat_interval > 0` and `(failure_count - 1) % repeat_interval == 0`
AND the bead does not have a `mitosis-depth:*` label. Keep the existing early-return pattern.

### 3. Unit tests in `src/mitosis/mod.rs`

- `repeat_interval_triggers_at_correct_counts`: fires at 1, 1+N, 1+2N; skips all others
- `repeat_interval_skips_max_depth_beads`: bead with `mitosis-depth:1` label + repeat tick → skipped
- `repeat_interval_zero_preserves_first_failure_only`: interval=0, first_failure_only=true → only fires at 1

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo fmt` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- All existing mitosis tests pass
- New unit tests pass
- Config `[mitosis]\nrepeat_interval = 50` causes re-split at failure 51, 101, etc.

title: mitosis: dedup only checks direct children of the CURRENT parent, invisible to duplicates from earlier/other generations in the same cascade
description:
src/mitosis/mod.rs:428-465 (get_existing_children) discovers dedup candidates by filtering list_all() for the label parent-<this_specific_bead_id> -- i.e. ONLY beads that are direct children of the bead currently being split. In a multi-generation cascade (bf-oeotj -> child A -> grandchild B -> great-grandchild C -> ...), when C is being split, dedup only sees C's own future direct children -- it has zero visibility into what A, B, or their OTHER children already proposed/covered. Confirmed empirically: 7 near-duplicate leaf beads survived across different immediate parents in the same lineage (see epic bf-iu3ao for the full list) precisely because none of them shared a common immediate parent.

Fix: tag every mitosis descendant with a lineage-root label at creation time, e.g. root-<original_bead_id> (propagate from parent's own root-* label if present, else parent.id if parent is the un-split original) -- cheap flat label lookup, no tree walk needed. Change get_existing_children (or add a sibling function) to gather ALL beads sharing the same root-<id> label, not just parent-<this_id>, and dedup new proposals against that full set.

Depends conceptually on bf-3ao9f (depth tracking) for the SAME root label propagation mechanism -- consider implementing both label additions (root-* and the corrected mitosis-depth:N) in the same pass through create_children since they touch the same code path, but they are independently testable/acceptance-checkable.

Acceptance:
- A proposed child at generation 4 that duplicates (exact title match) a bead created at generation 2 in the same lineage is correctly skipped as a dup.
- Dedup does NOT cross into an unrelated lineage (a bead from a different root's cascade with the same title is not skipped -- root-scoping must be genuinely scoped, not global).
- Existing single-generation dedup tests (create_children_with_dedup, create_children_all_deduped, dedup_ignores_children_of_other_parents) still pass.
close_reason:
Lineage-wide dedup for mitosis has been successfully implemented and tested.

## Implementation Summary

Fixed the mitosis dedup logic that only checked direct children of the current parent by implementing lineage-wide tracking:

### Core Changes
- Added root label to track mitosis lineage across generations
- Added extract_root_label() function to propagate root labels from parent to children
- Added get_lineage_beads() function to gather all beads sharing the same root label
- Modified create_children() to dedup against BOTH direct children AND entire lineage

### Acceptance Criteria Met
- Generation 4 child duplicating generation 2 bead is correctly skipped
- Dedup does NOT cross into unrelated lineages (different root labels)
- All existing single-generation dedup tests still pass (33/33 tests passing)

### Tests Added
- multi_generation_dedup_prevents_duplicates_across_lineage - validates cross-generation dedup
- dedup_does_not_cross_unrelated_lineages - validates lineage scoping
- root_label_propagates_from_parent_to_child - validates root label propagation
- root_bead_creates_root_label_for_children - validates root label creation

title: Config paths with literal ~ are not tilde-expanded — creates literal ./~/ dir in workspace
description:
## Problem
A literal directory named '~' exists at the repo root (see ~/.needle/state/heartbeats, ~/.needle/state/workers.json, pulse/reflect/weave state under it — all relative to the workspace root, i.e. a directory literally named tilde). Cause: the 'needle init' config template (src/cli/mod.rs, ~line 1293) writes 'home: ~/.needle' under 'workspace:', and the config loader (src/config/mod.rs) never expands a leading '~/' in path-typed config values — grep confirms no tilde/expand logic exists. YAML '~/.needle' therefore becomes a relative path, so every worker creates a literal '~' tree in its cwd. Built-in defaults use dirs_or_home() (src/config/mod.rs ~line 2153) which reads HOME correctly, so only file/env-provided paths are affected.

## Impact
Heartbeat files, worker registry, and strand state land in per-cwd literal '~' dirs instead of the real HOME, silently breaking peer heartbeat visibility, stale-claim cleanup, and splice detection across workers with different cwds. Relates to plan.md 'Concurrency > Heartbeat Protocol' (heartbeat_dir default ~/.needle/state/heartbeats/) and 'Configuration' chapter.

## Fix
1. Add tilde expansion (leading '~/' -> HOME) applied uniformly to all path-typed config fields on load (workspace.home, heartbeat_dir, adapters_dir, canary_workspace, telemetry paths, etc.) in src/config/mod.rs.
2. Keep 'needle init' template as-is (now safe) or switch it to write the absolute path.
3. 'needle doctor' should warn when a literal './~' directory exists in the workspace.
4. Delete the stray literal '~' directory from the NEEDLE repo root (it is untracked) and add '~/' to .gitignore as a guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests: '~/.needle' in global config, workspace .needle.yaml, and env var all resolve under HOME; bare '~' and '~/x' handled; paths without tilde unchanged; missing HOME falls back sanely.
- Running a worker from any cwd with the init-generated config creates state under HOME, never a literal ./~/.
- needle doctor flags an existing literal ./~ dir.
- cargo clippy clean; no unwrap/expect in non-test code.

title: P7.1a Fix cmd_cleanup liveness check: tree-walk PID instead of comparing raw pane_pid
description: cmd_cleanup's no-flags liveness check (src/cli/mod.rs, filter_sessions_for_cleanup) compares TmuxSession.pid (tmux #{pane_pid}, the pane's shell PID) against scan_needle_processes()'s PID set, which deliberately EXCLUDES shell-wrapper PIDs by design. Verified empirically 2026-07-21 by reproducing NEEDLE's exact launch shape (tmux new-session -d -s <name> "NEEDLE_INNER=1 <exe> <args> 2>> <log>"): pane_pid is always the bash -c wrapper; the real needle process is a CHILD with a different PID (output redirection defeats bash's exec-optimization). So the containment check is false for every genuinely live tmux-launched session, always -- bare 'needle cleanup' still classifies every live session as orphaned, reproducing the 2026-07-19 incident it was supposed to fix. Fix: reuse find_needle_process_in_tree() (src/cli/mod.rs, already used correctly by cmd_stop) to walk from pane_pid to the actual needle run descendant before checking liveness, instead of comparing pane_pid directly. Full writeup: docs/adr/003-cleanup-orphan-detection-gap.md Addendum (2026-07-21), plan.md Phase 7 section 7.1a.

title: Explore strand still exits after first workspace — reopen bf-4feux false close, fix AND redeploy
description:
REOPENS the explore roaming defect. bf-4feux ("Implement workspace iteration fix in
explore.rs") is CLOSED, but the fix never landed and the bug is live in production as of
2026-07-25. This bead exists to (a) record the false close with line-level proof and
(b) require a REDEPLOY, which the earlier beads do not cover.

## Proof the fix is absent from HEAD (295f92a, 2026-07-24)

src/strand/explore.rs:538   for workspace in &workspaces {
src/strand/explore.rs:756       return StrandResult::BeadFound(candidates);
src/strand/explore.rs:768   }   <- loop closes AFTER the return

The return at :756 is INSIDE the loop, directly after the tracing::info! that emits
"explore found candidates in remote workspace". So the strand still exits on the FIRST
workspace with a non-empty pre-filter candidate list and never scans the rest. This is
exactly the mechanism root-caused in bf-4df1e on 2026-07-19; nothing about it changed.

## Still reproduces under the NEW config, so bf-1nvkj did not resolve it

bf-4df1e was written against an explicit 24-repo explore.workspaces list. That list is now
empty (explore.workspaces: []) with workspace_root: /home/coding/ and recursive discovery
finding total_workspaces=36. The defect is unchanged under recursive discovery.

Live capture from worker claude-code-glm-4.7-h5-adc, 2026-07-26T02:04Z:

  explore: worker scan rotation: starting at workspace index 26 total_workspaces=36
  explore: explore found candidates in remote workspace workspace=<repo>/AgentScribe candidates=4
  strand:  strand found candidates strand=explore candidates=0 excluded=4 elapsed_ms=9
  worker:  state transition from=SELECTING to=EXHAUSTED
  worker:  all strands exhausted, waiting before retry backoff_secs=900

Explore checked 1 of 36 workspaces, returned 4 candidates, the outer waterfall in
src/strand/mod.rs excluded all 4 via pluck.exclude_labels, and the worker declared TOTAL
exhaustion and slept 900s -- never reaching spaxel (16 ready) or drawrace (15 ready).

## Production impact measured 2026-07-25

- Worker h5-adc: 0 beads processed in 15.5 hours, 50,202 heartbeats, ~12.7 percent CPU
  burned on an empty idle loop, 66 MB of stderr.
- Worker h8-roam: 56 beads total, all from the bare-home store, which now has 0 ready.
- Worker h7-mobile: seeded to a 0-ready repo, EXHAUSTED, never left it across 11,775
  log records -- proving -w is a HARD PIN in practice, not a seed.
- Net effect: roaming does not work at all. Every worker must be manually pinned with -w
  to a repo with verified ready beads, or it is dead weight.

## Deployment gap (not covered by bf-4df1e or bf-633fk)

Deployed binary is needle 0.2.12, installed 2026-07-20 16:57. Repo HEAD is 2026-07-24.
The running fleet is 4 days behind HEAD, so landing the code fix is necessary but NOT
sufficient -- the binary must be rebuilt and redeployed to the lab fleet.

## Acceptance criteria

1. explore.rs accumulates candidates ACROSS all workspaces in a scan, or at minimum
   continues to the next workspace when the current one yields zero post-exclusion
   candidates. No early return on first non-empty pre-filter list.
2. The exclusion set applied by the outer waterfall (src/strand/mod.rs) is applied
   BEFORE explore decides it has found something, so "candidates=4 -> excluded=4" can
   never be reported as a successful find.
3. Regression test: a fleet of N workspaces where workspace[0] yields only excluded
   candidates and workspace[N-1] has a genuinely ready bead -- the strand must return
   the bead from workspace[N-1].
4. Rebuild and redeploy the binary to the lab fleet, then VERIFY on a live worker that
   it roams to a second workspace. Follow the documented hot-reload semantics: replace
   only needle-stable, and do not mv over the spawn path of running workers.
5. Verified by observation, not assertion: capture a log line showing one worker
   processing beads from two different workspaces in a single session.

## Do not close without item 5

bf-4feux was closed without the code change landing. Do not repeat that. Closing this
bead requires a pasted log excerpt showing cross-workspace bead processing on the live
fleet.

title: mitosis: titles_match dedup is pure substring/exact matching, misses semantically-identical children phrased with different verbs
description:
src/mitosis/mod.rs:554-564 (titles_match):

  let normalize = |s: &str| -> String {
      s.trim().trim_start_matches(|c: char| !c.is_alphabetic()).to_lowercase()
  };
  let e = normalize(existing);
  let p = normalize(proposed);
  e == p || e.contains(&p) || p.contains(&e)

This only catches exact-after-normalization matches or one title being a literal substring of the other. Confirmed empirically these three real, distinct-parent sibling proposals from the same cascade all check the IDENTICAL underlying fact (EMA reads weekly_scoped_pct, not the deprecated sonnet_pct) but NONE match under this function, since none is a substring of another:
  - \"Verify EMA calculation uses model-agnostic weekly_scoped_pct\"
  - \"Confirm EMA calculation uses weekly_scoped_pct not sonnet_pct\"
  - \"Validate rotated model percentage feeds EMA correctly\"
An LLM proposing mitosis children naturally varies verbs (verify/confirm/validate/check/ensure) and word order across split rounds -- pure substring matching will keep missing this class of duplicate even after bf-3mfgf (dedup scope) fixes WHICH beads get compared.

Fix: replace or supplement titles_match with a looser similarity check before falling back to \"not a duplicate\" -- e.g. token-set (bag of words) overlap / Jaccard similarity above a tuned threshold, first stripping a small stopword+common-verb list (verify, confirm, validate, check, ensure, the, a, that, uses, not, etc.) so \"verify X uses Y\" and \"confirm X uses Y not Z\" collapse to comparable token sets. Keep the existing exact/substring check as a fast-path; add the fuzzy check as a fallback, not a replacement (avoid a network/embedding-API call here -- this needs to stay fast and offline, called synchronously in the mitosis evaluate path).

Acceptance:
- The three real titles above are recognized as duplicates of each other under the new check.
- Existing exact/substring test cases (titles_match_exact, titles_match_substring, titles_no_match) still pass.
- A deliberately-unrelated pair of titles from real cascades (pick two genuinely distinct beads from this epic's source lineage, e.g. \"Update documentation and close parent bead\" vs \"Run cargo test to verify no regressions\") is NOT falsely flagged as a duplicate -- tune the threshold against this as a negative control, not just the positive one above.

title: Explore strand stops scanning at the first workspace with any candidates, never reaching later workspaces in the list
description:
Root-caused via a 2-hour reproduction on the live lab fleet (2026-07-19): 6 freshly-launched roaming workers (workspace equals /home/coding) each processed ZERO beads across roughly 6 selection cycles spanning 19:00 to 20:46, despite ~250 genuinely ready beads sitting across ~18 other repos unlocked earlier the same day via a doctor --reclaim-stale sweep.

MECHANISM (src/strand/explore.rs, the main for workspace in and workspaces loop, roughly lines 314 to 470): the loop iterates the configured explore.workspaces list in order. As soon as it finds ANY workspace whose post-filter candidate list is non-empty, it calls return StrandResult BeadFound candidates immediately -- it does not continue scanning the remaining workspaces in that same invocation, and does not aggregate or compare candidates across multiple workspaces.

Two repos into the current 24-repo explore.workspaces list is HOOP, which has exactly one open bead (bf-4jleu) carrying a stale assignee from a retired worker identity (claude-code-glm-4.7-alpha). Explore own defensive retain filter (checking b.assignee.is_none()) fails to catch this, because bf ready --format json omits the assignee field from its JSON output entirely (confirmed directly: the JSON for bf-4jleu has no assignee key at all, though bf show correctly reports one) -- see the companion bead filed in bead-forge for this schema gap. So explore treats bf-4jleu as a legitimate candidate, returns early with BeadFound, and stops scanning workspaces 3 through 24 entirely for that cycle.

The outer waterfall (src/strand/mod.rs, around line 335-390) then applies its OWN, separate exclusion check (a per-session set of previously-failed bead IDs, e.g. race-lost claims) and correctly filters bf-4jleu out -- producing the observed log line strand found candidates strand=explore candidates=0 excluded=1 -- but by then explore.rs has already returned, so the wrapper just falls through to the NEXT STRAND TYPE in the waterfall (weave, unravel, etc), not the next workspace. The remaining 22 workspaces, several with dozens of genuinely ready beads, are never checked in that cycle.

Net effect: a single stale-assigned bead in an early-ordered workspace can silently starve the entire roaming fleet, indefinitely, with no error surfaced anywhere obvious -- the logs read as healthy activity (explore found candidates, strand found candidates) right up until the point nothing actually gets dispatched.

ACCEPTANCE:
- explore.rs continue scanning remaining workspaces in the SAME invocation after a workspace candidate list turns out to be unusable (post outer-wrapper exclusion filtering), instead of returning after the first non-empty result and waiting for the next full waterfall cycle to retry.
- Add a regression test: workspace 1 in the list has a candidate that will be excluded by the outer wrapper filter (not caught by explore own retain), workspace 2 has a genuinely claimable candidate -- explore should return workspace 2 candidate in the SAME cycle, not stall.
- Consider whether explore should aggregate/rank candidates across ALL workspaces before returning, rather than first-match-wins by list order, so a single bad bead early in the configured list can never fully block later workspaces.

I did not attempt a source fix myself -- flagging for implementation. I also tried and failed to manually clear bf-4jleu stale assignee as a stopgap (three attempts via bf claim plus reclaim-stale all raced to a different bead due to live worker contention); did not force it further to avoid interfering with the live fleet.
close_reason: Fixed in origin/main 73635f7 (CI needle-ci-mrskq Succeeded): explore scans ALL workspaces and aggregates candidates, ranks globally, no early return; regression test aggregates_candidates_across_all_workspaces.

title: Mend strand calls nonexistent br/bf release command every cycle, breaking orphan cleanup fleet-wide
description: The Mend strand shells out to `br release <bead-id>` to reset orphaned in_progress beads (assignee has no live worker) back to open. That subcommand does not exist in current bead-forge: both `bf release` and `br release` return error: unrecognized subcommand release (tip: delete). Confirmed live via the cgov roaming worker stderr log on 2026-07-19 — it fails identically every ~17-minute idle cycle (needle::strand::mend: failed to release orphaned in-progress bead ... error=br release bf-3q0yf failed), meaning Mend has been silently non-functional for as long as this code path has existed. Impact was severe: a manual fleet-wide sweep using the ACTUALLY working mechanism (bf doctor --reclaim-stale --ttl 60) found and released 173 orphaned in_progress beads across 18 repos that Mend should have been cleaning up automatically (spot check: NEEDLE itself had 30, SIGIL 12, aide-de-camp 13, zai-proxy 13). Fix: change Mend to shell out to bf doctor --reclaim-stale -w <workspace> --ttl <N> instead of the nonexistent release subcommand, or add a bf release <id> alias to bead-forge if per-bead targeting is actually required. Related gap filed in bead-forge: see the bead-forge repo bug about no CLI mechanism to clear assignee on an already-open bead (a second, distinct issue also discovered during this audit).

title: Implement 'needle config --set KEY VALUE' per plan Binary Structure
description:

title: tmux-wrapped workers on lab die silently at worker_construction; NEEDLE_INNER=1 direct launch works
description: Reproduced 2026-07-19 on lab, twice (armor-p6c, armor-p6d): needle run -w ~/ARMOR -a claude-code-glm-5 -i X reports Started worker in tmux session, but the inner process dies within seconds - stderr log ends mid worker_construction (last line is the learning-entry too-few-lines WARN), no panic, no claim, tmux session gone. System load was ~1 at launch time, binary unchanged since Jul 10, 3 older tmux fleet workers unaffected. Suspect the tmux-session spawn path (env/pty/cgroup of NEW tmux sessions) rather than needle logic. Workaround documented in ops memory: launch with setsid nohup env NEEDLE_INNER=1 needle run ... outside tmux. Related: bf-1dwyq (duplicate dispatch), bf-hzblx (process tracking).

title: Audit all tokio::time::timeout-wrapped process spawns for missing kill_on_drop
description:
This mitosis-evaluation leak is the second known instance of this bug class in NEEDLE (the first was issue #8/ADR-009's CommandGate, already fixed with kill_on_drop). Grep the whole crate for tokio::time::timeout(...) wrapping any call chain that ends in a process spawn, and verify kill_on_drop(true) is set on each.

Known candidates to check beyond mitosis:
- strand/weave.rs's WEAVE_STRAND_TIMEOUT_SECS (120s, src/strand/weave.rs:574-581) -- check if it wraps a dispatch call with the same gap.
- worker/mod.rs's commit-hook timeout (immediately after the mitosis block, ~line 2430) -- check similarly.
- Any other strand (mend, explore, pluck) that dispatches an agent under a timeout.

Fix each finding the same way as the mitosis fix (kill_on_drop(true) + async tokio::process::Command), and add a regression test per site following the pattern established by this bug's own test bead.
close_reason: Audited all tokio::time::timeout-wrapped spawns: weave strand had the same gap (fixed, confirmed reachable via same outer-timeout shape), commit_hook.rs git spawns hardened with kill_on_drop as lower-risk follow-on, mend/explore/pluck strands not applicable (no timeout-wrapped spawns). See ADR-011.

title: Genesis: Pluck Telemetry Isolation & Fleet Process Tracking (Phase 6)
description:
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md, Phase 6 section. ADR-002 in docs/adr/ (pluck telemetry isolation and process tracking).

Overview: Pluck currently writes its own starvation self-diagnostic as a bead into whatever workspace it is scanning, instead of into NEEDLE own telemetry. On ~/ARMOR this produced an unresolvable bead (its fix target was NEEDLE own unreachable config) that spiraled into 346 fabricated beads and ~2300 wasted bead-cycles over 8 days. Separately, needle stop/status/list were found to have process-tracking blind spots during remediation (a stopped worker kept running; another worker was invisible to both commands entirely).

Progress:
- [ ] 6.1 Pluck telemetry isolation
- [ ] 6.2 Fleet process tracking
- [ ] 6.3/6.4 Regression tests + deployment (folded into each child beads acceptance criteria)

Closes out the incident documented in bf-hzblx (closed, superseded by this genesis and ADR).

title: Investigate and fix 237-second stall in weave strand bf list --json call
description:
Found 2026-07-15 dispatching roaming workers into ~/NEEDLE + ~/ARMOR: weave strand took 237614ms (237.6s) to fail with the exact same error (bead store error: bf list --json failed) that mend, unravel, and knot all hit near-instantly (0-63ms) in the SAME selection cycle, against the SAME underlying store, moments apart.

Exact timings from one worker.exhausted event strand_evaluations array:
pluck: error, 1ms
mend: error, 63ms
explore: bead_found(1), 4ms
weave: error, 237614ms  <- the outlier
unravel: error, 1ms
pulse: no_work, 0ms
reflect: error, 0ms
splice: no_work, 0ms
knot: error, 1ms

This is not the store itself being generally slow - three other strands got a fast failure against it in the same cycle. Something specific to weaves invocation path differs: different args, an internal retry-with-backoff loop, a lock it waits on that the others do not, a much larger query/payload, or similar.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Identify what weave actually does differently in its bf list --json invocation vs mend/unravel/knots (check src/strand/weave.rs against the others).
- Reproduce the stall or identify the exact code path responsible.
- Add a bounded timeout so a single strand cannot stall an entire SELECTING cycle for minutes - a worker going from finding a real candidate (explore succeeded) to EXHAUSTED should not take 4 minutes dominated by one strand hanging.
- Fix the root cause once identified, not just paper over it with a timeout.
close_reason: Successfully fixed the 237-second stall in weave strand evaluation. Root cause: no strand-level timeout allowed bead store recovery (30s + 60s sync + 30s retry = 120s) to run multiple times while other strands failed immediately. Fix: added 120s strand-level timeout using WEAVE_STRAND_TIMEOUT_SECS, plus 45s timeout for list_all() call. Returns NoWork on timeout instead of hanging, preventing SELECTING cycle stall. Code compiles successfully and follows existing timeout patterns.

title: Decide whether workspace discovery should re-run periodically, not just once at worker construction
description:
ExploreStrand::new()'s own doc comment: The workspace list is captured at construction time and never re-read. Even after 8.1/8.2 land, a long-lived roaming worker will not see a repo created after it started, without a restart.

This is an open design question, not a confirmed bug -- flagging for a decision rather than prescribing a fix. Options include: periodic re-discovery on an interval, re-discovery triggered by an external signal, or accepting restart-to-pick-up-new-repos as adequate given workers already cycle relatively often in this fleet.

See plan.md Phase 8.3.

title: P10.3/10.4 Mend: unconditional reclamation per supervisor tick + release stale assignee on Open beads
description: Two compounding gaps: (1) Mend is only reachable inside a live worker's own waterfall loop (Strand 2) -- needle supervise's tick() (src/supervisor/mod.rs:262-331) never calls it and only spawns a worker when ready_beads is non-empty, so a fully idle fleet holding only stale claims can never trigger a spawn, which means Mend never runs, which means the stale claims never clear -- a closed loop with no external kick. Fix: tick() must call a mend-equivalent reclamation pass UNCONDITIONALLY every tick, before (not gated by) the ready_beads check. Also add the same reclamation to 'needle doctor --repair' as a standalone path independent of any worker/supervisor. (2) This is Phase 5.2's original, never-implemented promise: cleanup_orphaned_in_progress (src/strand/mend.rs:68) only handles status==InProgress -- add a sibling function that releases the assignee on any Open bead whose assignee has no live heartbeat, per ADR-001's documented gap. BLOCKS ON bf-4j9pr: Mend's actual release call currently shells out to a nonexistent 'br release' subcommand and has been silently non-functional -- bf-4j9pr's own diagnosis (shell out to 'bf doctor --reclaim-stale -w <workspace> --ttl <N>' instead) should be the release mechanism this bead builds on, not a second broken implementation. title: Mitosis evaluation timeout leaks orphaned claude child process, never reaped
description:
tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(120), self.mitosis_evaluator.evaluate(...)) in src/worker/mod.rs (~line 2355) drops the inner future on timeout without killing the underlying claude subprocess it spawned. Dropping a Tokio future mid-Child::wait() does not kill the OS process -- none of mitosis/mod.rs, dispatch/mod.rs, or worker/mod.rs set kill_on_drop(true) on that spawn path (grep confirms zero hits), unlike the CommandGate fix already shipped for issue #8/ADR-009, which added kill_on_drop(true) + async tokio::process::Command specifically to solve this same class of problem elsewhere in the codebase.

Confirmed live on lab (100.81.129.38) 2026-07-30/31: warden-p1's mitosis evaluation for beads wd-1sk and wd-3oc timed out on 5 of 5 observed attempts over a 2+ hour span, each leaking one more 'claude --disallowed-tools spawn_worker' orphan process. Fleet-wide, 'mitosis: dispatching agent' fires constantly (grep counts up to 456 in one worker log, 100-400 in a dozen others). This is what caused two full-fleet collapses tonight: a single worker's leaked-children process tree grew to 146 descendants (warden-p1) and separately 74 descendants (claude-print-opus-alpha) within minutes of being observed; killing either tree took the shared tmux server down with it (that process happened to be the one hosting the server on a clean boot), killing all 16 registered workers both times. Load average hit 248-308 on a 12-core box during both incidents.

This is DISTINCT from GitHub issue #12 (Supervisor::spawn_worker under needle supervise never reaping workers -- ADR-010 explicitly scopes that fix as not applying to needle run single-worker mode). This bug lives in Worker's own per-bead dispatch loop and reproduces under plain needle run, which is the mode every pinned/roaming worker on lab actually runs in -- ADR-010's 'not needle run' scoping assumption is incomplete.

Evidence:
- src/worker/mod.rs:~2355 -- tokio::time::timeout wrapping mitosis_evaluator.evaluate(), the Err(_) timeout branch just logs a warning and continues, never touches the spawned child.
- src/mitosis/mod.rs:343 -- .dispatch(&bead.id, &prompt, adapter, workspace) call inside evaluate(), the spawn path with no kill_on_drop.
- grep -rn kill_on_drop src/mitosis/mod.rs src/dispatch/mod.rs src/worker/mod.rs -> zero hits.
- needle-claude-code-glm-4_7-warden-p1.stderr.log: repeated 'mitosis evaluation timed out after 120s, continuing to LOGGING' for wd-1sk (21:16, 21:21, 22:10, 22:27 UTC) and wd-3oc (01:33 UTC) on 2026-07-30/31, 5/5 timeout rate observed for those two beads.
- Live process counts during incident: warden-p1's tree reached 146 descendants, claude-print-opus-alpha reached 74, both entirely 'claude --disallowed-tools spawn_worker' children at cwd matching the parent worker's own launch context.
close_reason: Fixed, tested, and released as v0.2.14 (https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/tag/v0.2.14). Verified via full local test suite (1629+4 tests, 0 failures, iad-ci unavailable due to separate node-pool issue) and red/green regression test. Root cause + fix documented in ADR-011, GH issue #13.

title: P12.1/12.3 Gate worker_construction and needle-supervise auto-scale spawn on check_system_resources()
description: check_system_resources() is only called from do_dispatch() (src/worker/mod.rs:1607-1612) -- an already-running worker about to execute an already-claimed bead. It is never consulted before or during worker_construction (src/cli/mod.rs:861-868, a plain init_step with no resource gate) and never during needle supervise's auto-scale spawn path (src/supervisor/mod.rs). NEEDLE's own 60s boot timeout (src/cli/mod.rs:870-875) evaluates only after init_step returns and structurally cannot catch a process killed mid-step by external CPU pressure. Fix: call check_system_resources() (generalized beyond its current rate-limit-specific naming) before entering worker_construction, from BOTH the CLI launch path and the supervisor's auto-scale path (shared implementation). If saturated, retry with bounded backoff instead of proceeding into the ~5s construction step; fail explicitly with a named reason if still saturated after a max wait, instead of letting the OS silently kill it. Related, complementary: bf-56gwl (documents the same symptom with a tmux-spawn-path hypothesis -- not mutually exclusive with the CPU-saturation hypothesis this fix targets; land this regardless). See plan.md Phase 12 sections 12.1/12.3, ADR-008.

Both paths use shared RateLimiter::check_system_resources_for_launch() with: 120s max wait, exponential backoff (5s→30s cap), explicit failure with clear error messages, telemetry emission (WorkerLaunchDeferred, SupervisorSpawnFailed). Verification documented in notes/bf-670a3.md. Implementation matches ADR-008 requirements.

title: Test tmux fixtures kill production fleet via unscoped default-socket kill-session by needle- prefix
description:
ROOT CAUSE of repeated whole-fleet collapses (2026-07-11, 2026-07-27 x2, 2026-07-28), confirmed live on lab (100.81.129.38):

tests/tmux_fixture.rs uses bare Command::new("tmux") with NO -L <socket> isolation for
list_all_sessions(), list_needle_sessions() (filters session_name.starts_with("needle-")),
kill_sessions_with_prefix(prefix), and TmuxSession::kill()/Drop. Same for
tests/cleanup_liveness_regression.rs kill_session(). All of these operate on the
DEFAULT tmux socket -- the exact same socket real needle run production workers and
the users own interactive tmux sessions live on.

Production worker sessions are named needle-claude-code-glm-4_7-<identifier> and the
supervisor session is needle-supervisor -- both match the "needle-" prefix these test
helpers filter/kill on. Any test that calls kill_sessions_with_prefix("needle-") (or similar)
as setup/teardown cleanup will kill the ENTIRE live production fleet in one shot, while
leaving non-"needle-"-prefixed sessions (e.g. an operators bare-named tmux sessions) untouched
-- this exact signature (simultaneous SIGHUP across every needle-* session, non-needle sessions
unaffected) is what was observed in every collapse incident to date.

Confirmed live 2026-07-28: two integration tests, exhaustion_empty_workspace and
debug_worker_hang --nocapture, were found HUNG for 23+ hours (since 2026-07-27 15:31/15:41 EDT,
started by a prior claude session running cargo test ... --test integration_tests). Within
minutes of a fresh 6-worker production fleet being launched, all 6 production sessions +
needle-supervisor died via SIGHUP in a ~7min staggered window (18:23:38-18:30:49 UTC) while
3 bare-named operator tmux sessions on the same server were completely unaffected -- textbook
match for this bug. The two hung processes were killed manually (SIGINT then SIGKILL) as an
immediate mitigation; this bead tracks the actual fix.

FIX NEEDED:
1. Give every test-spawned tmux session its own isolated socket (tmux -L needle-test-<pid>
   or similar) instead of touching the default socket at all -- this is the real fix, since it
   makes test cleanup structurally incapable of reaching production sessions regardless of
   naming.
2. Belt-and-suspenders: rename the test-only session prefix to something that can never
   collide with production naming (e.g. "needle-itest-" instead of relying on "needle-"), and
   make list_needle_sessions()/kill_sessions_with_prefix() require an exact adapter+identifier
   match rather than a bare prefix.
3. Add a test-suite-level guard/lint that fails CI if any test constructs a bare
   Command::new("tmux") without an explicit -L argument.
4. Separately: whatever caused these two tests to hang for 23h instead of completing/timing out
   is its own bug worth a follow-up (test harness has no timeout enforcement) -- not the same
   bug as the kill-prefix issue, but the hang is what let a normally-fast cleanup call sit
   around as a live landmine for a full day.

Related: the 2026-07-27 collapse postmortem already flagged this exact mechanism as an
"unconfirmed lead" (stray integration_tests-* processes present near collapse time, same
~/.needle/logs/ dir shared with fixture logs) -- this bead confirms it with source-level proof
(tmux_fixture.rs:305 kill_sessions_with_prefix, default socket, "needle-" prefix match) plus a
live repro. Do not close without a code fix landing AND a redeploy verified not to recur (same
bar as bf-47bfm/bf-24dpc's "no closing without live-log proof" clause).

title: Distinguish no home bead store from genuine strand errors in telemetry
description:
A roaming worker dispatched with -w /home/coding (bare parent, no .beads/ of its own) shows 6 of 9 strands (pluck, mend, weave, unravel, reflect, knot) reporting error every single cycle - not no_work, actual error - because bf list/bf list --json fails outright against a workspace with no valid bead store. Only explore (which targets a separate configured workspaces list, not home) and pulse/splice (which apparently degrade gracefully) return something other than error.

This makes worker.exhausted telemetry misleading: a pure-roam worker behaving exactly as designed will ALWAYS show two-thirds of its strands erroring, indistinguishable from a worker hitting genuine failures against a real, valid store. Directly caused confusion diagnosing a live incident 2026-07-15 - had to cross-reference raw stderr logs to tell apart no home store configured (expected, benign) from actual bugs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Detect missing/invalid home bead store (no .beads/ dir, or workspace intentionally unset for roam-only workers) as a distinct, clean result - e.g. no_home_store or skipped - separate from error.
- Reserve error strictly for genuine failures against a store that does exist (corruption, lock contention, CLI crash, etc).
- worker.exhausted and strand.evaluated telemetry should make it trivial to tell this worker has no home store by design apart from this worker home store is broken at a glance, without needing to grep raw stderr.
- Regression test: a worker configured with no home .beads/ produces no_home_store (or equivalent) for pluck/mend/weave/unravel/reflect/knot, not error.

title: Emit structured fleet.cpu_saturated and fleet.memory_low telemetry events
description:
The plan specifies (Concurrency section, Fleet Sizing) that NEEDLE emits a `fleet.cpu_saturated` event when system load exceeds `cpu_load_warn` threshold, and implies a corresponding memory warning event.

Currently `check_system_resources()` in `src/rate_limit/mod.rs` uses `tracing::warn!` log macros rather than structured telemetry events. This violates design principle 4 (Observable by default: every state transition emits structured telemetry) and the plan's event catalog is incomplete without these events.

## Deliverables
- Add `FleetCpuSaturated { load_average: f64, threshold: f64, core_count: usize }` variant to `EventKind` in `src/telemetry/mod.rs`
- Add `FleetMemoryLow { free_mb: u64, threshold_mb: u64 }` variant to `EventKind`
- Update `check_system_resources()` in `src/rate_limit/mod.rs` to accept a `&Telemetry` sink and emit these events instead of (or in addition to) the tracing log
- Update call sites in `src/worker/mod.rs` to pass the telemetry sink
- Add the two event types to the telemetry documentation in `docs/plan/plan.md` (Health event catalog)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `fleet.cpu_saturated` event appears in JSONL log when load exceeds threshold
- [ ] `fleet.memory_low` event appears in JSONL log when free RAM drops below threshold
- [ ] Both events carry the numeric values (actual vs threshold) in their `data` field
- [ ] Events are exported via OTLP sink (severity WARN)

title: Mitosis evaluation timeout leaks orphaned claude child process, never reaped
description:
tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(120), self.mitosis_evaluator.evaluate(...)) in src/worker/mod.rs (~line 2355) drops the inner future on timeout without killing the underlying claude subprocess it spawned. Dropping a Tokio future mid-Child::wait() does not kill the OS process -- none of mitosis/mod.rs, dispatch/mod.rs, or worker/mod.rs set kill_on_drop(true) on that spawn path (grep confirms zero hits), unlike the CommandGate fix already shipped for issue #8/ADR-009, which added kill_on_drop(true) + async tokio::process::Command specifically to solve this same class of problem elsewhere in the codebase.

Confirmed live on lab (100.81.129.38) 2026-07-30/31: warden-p1's mitosis evaluation for beads wd-1sk and wd-3oc timed out on 5 of 5 observed attempts over a 2+ hour span, each leaking one more 'claude --disallowed-tools spawn_worker' orphan process. Fleet-wide, 'mitosis: dispatching agent' fires constantly (grep counts up to 456 in one worker log, 100-400 in a dozen others). This is what caused two full-fleet collapses tonight: a single worker's leaked-children process tree grew to 146 descendants (warden-p1) and separately 74 descendants (claude-print-opus-alpha) within minutes of being observed; killing either tree took the shared tmux server down with it (that process happened to be the one hosting the server on a clean boot), killing all 16 registered workers both times. Load average hit 248-308 on a 12-core box during both incidents.

This is DISTINCT from GitHub issue #12 (Supervisor::spawn_worker under needle supervise never reaping workers -- ADR-010 explicitly scopes that fix as not applying to needle run single-worker mode). This bug lives in Worker's own per-bead dispatch loop and reproduces under plain needle run, which is the mode every pinned/roaming worker on lab actually runs in -- ADR-010's 'not needle run' scoping assumption is incomplete.

Evidence:
- src/worker/mod.rs:~2355 -- tokio::time::timeout wrapping mitosis_evaluator.evaluate(), the Err(_) timeout branch just logs a warning and continues, never touches the spawned child.
- src/mitosis/mod.rs:343 -- .dispatch(&bead.id, &prompt, adapter, workspace) call inside evaluate(), the spawn path with no kill_on_drop.
- grep -rn kill_on_drop src/mitosis/mod.rs src/dispatch/mod.rs src/worker/mod.rs -> zero hits.
- needle-claude-code-glm-4_7-warden-p1.stderr.log: repeated 'mitosis evaluation timed out after 120s, continuing to LOGGING' for wd-1sk (21:16, 21:21, 22:10, 22:27 UTC) and wd-3oc (01:33 UTC) on 2026-07-30/31, 5/5 timeout rate observed for those two beads.
- Live process counts during incident: warden-p1's tree reached 146 descendants, claude-print-opus-alpha reached 74, both entirely 'claude --disallowed-tools spawn_worker' children at cwd matching the parent worker's own launch context.
