title: Pluck starvation self-diagnostic writes into target repo bead tracker instead of NEEDLE telemetry
description:
When Pluck (src/strand/pluck.rs) scans a target workspace and finds beads it cannot dispatch, it currently writes a Starvation alert AS A BEAD into the TARGET REPOS OWN .beads/issues.jsonl (observed in ~/ARMOR, bead bf-3b64, created 2026-07-06T12:45:30Z: "Open beads exist but Pluck found none - possible configuration error").

This is a category error: the alert is about NEEDLE own dispatch logic, but it lands in the workspace being worked on, where a dispatched worker will naturally pick it up and try to investigate/fix it - except the actual fix target (Plucks own exclude_labels/filter/config) is not part of that repo and is not reachable or editable from within it. The fix step can never legitimately complete.

CONFIRMED IMPACT: on ~/ARMOR this produced a self-perpetuating loop. A worker did the standard investigate-fix-verify-monitor decomposition (bf-1loh/bf-36co/bf-5oik/bf-6bdj); the fix bead (bf-36co) stayed permanently blocked since there was nothing in-repo to fix. Because the alert never resolved, later sessions kept re-triggering it and re-investigating from scratch (Locate Pluck configuration files was independently recreated at least 3 times). One investigative thread guessed the unreachable config was YAML-formatted and pivoted into building a complete YAML/JSON/TOML parser library from scratch as a proxy task, which snowballed into a pytest-output-parsing tool, folded-scalar test matrices, and hundreds of near-duplicate beads over 8 days (2026-07-06 through 2026-07-14). Two workers (bravo: 1671 beads, echo: 566 beads, both largely consumed by this lineage) had to be killed; needle stop only detached their tmux session and left the underlying OS process (and a third, alpha, invisible to needle status/list entirely) still running and still writing files to the target repo. 346 fabricated beads were bulk-closed in ~/ARMOR to recover.

FIX: Pluck starvation/self-diagnostic alerts should go to NEEDLE own telemetry/logs (or a bead in the NEEDLE repo itself, or a structured event), never into the target workspace being scanned. Separately worth hardening: needle stop should reliably kill the full process tree, not just detach the tmux wrapper, and needle status/list should not have blind spots for workers that are still running.

title: Epic: mitosis dedup is scoped and matched too weakly, letting a split cascade balloon into redundant near-duplicate children
description:
Observed live 2026-07-26/27 on lab: a single real bead (jedarden/claude-governor bf-oeotj, \"generalize the hardcoded seven_day_sonnet window\") mitosis-split into a cascade at least 4-5 generations deep (bf-oeotj -> bf-4frc2c -> bf-676sby -> bf-39jlzk -> bf-1hqw9s -> bf-6c96mw -> bf-4zyawd -> {bf-2303oz, bf-4lm1zk, bf-2oz6wg, bf-3owyp9, bf-1cnwpe, bf-1od4i8, bf-6d7v5n, bf-2yoq5o, bf-1fh0y5, bf-13oi92, bf-5kf29, ...}), producing at least 7 confirmed near-duplicate leaf beads that all independently re-verified the SAME underlying fact (that weekly_scoped_pct, not the deprecated sonnet_pct, feeds the EMA calculation) with different verbs:
  - \"Verify EMA calculation uses model-agnostic weekly_scoped_pct\" (bf-3owyp9)
  - \"Confirm EMA calculation uses weekly_scoped_pct not sonnet_pct\" (bf-1od4i8)
  - \"Validate rotated model percentage feeds EMA correctly\" (bf-6d7v5n)
  - \"Verify weekly_scoped_pct populated from model-agnostic limits\" (bf-1cnwpe)
  - plus a duplicate \"Audit sonnet_pct field usage\" and two duplicate \"run cargo test\" beads.
All 7 had to be manually pruned by an operator via direct grep-against-source verification -- the fleet had no mechanism to converge on its own.

Root-caused to THREE independent, compounding gaps in ~/NEEDLE/src/mitosis/mod.rs (see child beads). This is a different failure mode than bf-1fj7f (handle_crash bypassing the failure-count circuit breaker) -- that bug is about failure-count never incrementing on crash; this bug is about mitosis's children ballooning even when failure-count DOES increment normally, because dedup can't see across generations and can't recognize paraphrased duplicates. Related prior sighting (self-resolved that time, not root-caused): needle_lab_loop_sweep_2026-07-24 vista incident, same src/mitosis/mod.rs SPLIT-children labeling logic.

Closes when all children are closed and a fresh multi-generation split (real or simulated) demonstrably converges without operator intervention.

title: Bead-Id trailer injection races under concurrent same-workspace dispatch
description:
commit_hook::inject_bead_id_trailer (src/commit_hook.rs) runs git commit --amend --no-edit --trailer Bead-Id:X on whatever commit is currently at HEAD after a successful dispatch. Its only safety check (src/worker/mod.rs around line 2079) is current_head != pre_dispatch_head - it never verifies the commit actually AT head right now is the one its own agent produced.

Each needle run is a fully separate OS process (confirmed via ps aux - no shared memory, no mutex). Two workers pointed at the same workspace (e.g. via -w pointing both at the same path, or a roaming worker overlapping a pinned one) have no coordination at all around this step.

RACE: worker A dispatch completes, commits (HEAD=A1). Before A reaches inject_bead_id_trailer, worker B also completes and commits (HEAD=B1, on top of A1). A now checks current_head(B1) != pre_dispatch_head(base) -> true -> amends HEAD, i.e. rewrites B1 with Bead-Id:A trailer. B1 commit hash changes, its actual content gets mislabeled as belonging to bead A, and HOOPs bead_commit_index (the whole reason this trailer exists, per this files own doc comment) is now wrong. Worker B, whose own pre_dispatch_head bookkeeping expected its own commit at that position, is also now operating against a rewritten commit it does not recognize.

Not a file-content collision (unlike ordinary concurrent edits) - this race exists even when the two beads touch completely disjoint files, because it is about WHICH commit is at HEAD, not what changed.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Add a short-lived per-workspace advisory lock (flock on e.g. <workspace>/.git/needle-trailer.lock) held only across the read-HEAD -> verify -> amend sequence inside inject_bead_id_trailer, not the whole dispatch. Bounded by the existing 10-30s subprocess timeouts, so cost to throughput is negligible even under concurrent dispatch.
- Inside the lock, verify the commit actually at HEAD corresponds to the calling beads own dispatch before amending - NEEDLE commit convention already puts the bead id in the subject line (fix(needle-XYZ): ...), so this is a cheap git log -1 --format=%s match against the bead id, not new plumbing. If HEAD does not match this bead, skip the amend (log a miss for retry/investigation) rather than mislabeling another beads commit.
- Regression test: two concurrent inject_bead_id_trailer calls in the same workspace (simulate via two threads/processes racing on the same repo fixture) never cross-tag each others commit.
- Follow-up (not required for this bead, note only): swap --amend for git notes add <verified-sha> instead of amending HEAD in place, since notes attach metadata without rewriting the commits hash and would work even if the target commit is no longer at HEAD by the time tagging happens. Bigger change (HOOP would need to read notes instead of trailers) - only pursue if the lock+identity-check combination proves insufficient in practice.

Found while evaluating whether it is safe to dispatch a second worker into ~/NEEDLE alongside an already-running one, same workspace, same branch.

description:
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md, Phase 7 section. ADR-003 in docs/adr/ (cleanup command orphan-detection gap).

Overview: needle cleanup's help text and doc comment both claim it removes only orphaned sessions (no active worker), but the implementation has no liveness check in its no-flags path -- an absent --identifier becomes an empty string that matches every session, making bare needle cleanup functionally identical to needle cleanup --all. Discovered 2026-07-19 during lab fleet remediation when bare needle cleanup killed a live, actively-executing worker (armor-p6a) and the fleet's own auto-scaling supervisor daemon (needle-supervisor), neither of which was orphaned.

Progress:

title: Splice strand's report_workspace unset in NEEDLE's own .needle.yaml — worker-failure escalation silently non-functional for self
description:
plan.md Phase 6 section 6.5 (backed by ADR-002 in docs/adr/) established that strands.splice.report_workspace must be a validated, set config value — otherwise Splice (src/strand/splice.rs) document_failure/document_live_loop silently no-op (tracing::debug! only, no bead created) whenever they detect a crashed or stuck worker. Closed bead bf-1ep7w implemented the fix at the code level: src/config/mod.rs (around line 2214-2221) now emits a boot-time tracing::warn! when strands.splice.enabled=true and report_workspace is None.

The gap: NEEDLE own live workspace config at .needle.yaml (repo root) still has strands.splice.enabled: true paired with strands.splice.report_workspace: null. This means every worker booted against this repo currently emits that boot WARN, and Splice never actually escalates a crashed/stuck worker for NEEDLE own fleet — the exact class of incident described in ADR-002 (8-day ARMOR retry-storm, 346 fabricated beads) would currently go undetected if it happened against NEEDLE itself.

Fix: per the ADR isolation rule (file escalation records in NEEDLE own workspace, never a targets), set strands.splice.report_workspace to the absolute path of this repo checkout in .needle.yaml — this path already has a live .beads/ store (bf -w <repo>/.beads works today), so no new bead store needs to be created. Do NOT point it at the workspace.home directory referenced elsewhere in the same config file — that directory has no .beads/ subdirectory and document_failure would still silently no-op (verified by listing it: no .beads dir present). After the change, verify a worker boot against this repo no longer emits the splice report_workspace WARN, and if a test harness exists for splice (see src/strand/splice.rs tests and tests/ for fixtures), run it to confirm a synthetic stuck-worker scenario now produces an escalation bead. This is a local YAML config-file edit only — no secrets, no cluster/production changes, fully reversible via git.

title: ExploreStrand: apply live worker exclusions before deciding a workspace has candidates
description:
Part of bf-47bfm -- this is the actual code fix for the cross-workspace deadlock (bf-47bfm acceptance criteria 1-2). Depends on bf-10x6y (exclusions must be passed into evaluate() first).

In src/strand/explore.rs per-workspace loop (around line 528-758), after the existing assignee/label retain-filter, ALSO filter out any candidate whose id is in the exclusions parameter now passed into evaluate(). Only decide a workspace has nothing claimable (continue to next workspace) once BOTH label/assignee filtering AND the worker live exclusion set have been applied -- not before.

This fixes the exact repro in bf-47bfm: worker scans workspace[0], strand-level filtering finds candidates, returns BeadFound, but the OUTER waterfall exclusion set (strand/mod.rs) throws all of them away -- and the worker declares total exhaustion instead of trying workspace[1]. After this change that exclusion check happens INSIDE explore own loop, so it advances instead.

Acceptance:
- A workspace whose only candidates are in the worker exclusion set is treated identically to a workspace with 0 ready beads (cross-workspace mend attempted, then continue to next workspace)
- Existing 3 deadlock tests (label/assignee scenarios) still pass unmodified
- No change to behavior when exclusions is empty

title: Add trace sanitization performance benchmark (Phase 4 success criterion)
description:
Phase 4 success criteria include: 'Keyword pre-filter (Aho-Corasick) skips irrelevant rules; sanitization adds <10ms per trace file.'

There is currently no benchmark or test that measures sanitization latency. The 222-rule gitleaks scan plus Aho-Corasick pre-filter is on the critical write path (runs synchronously before trace write) and must stay under 10ms per trace file.

## Deliverables
- Add a Criterion benchmark in `benches/sanitize.rs` (or equivalent) that:
  1. Generates representative trace file content (10KB, 100KB, 1MB) of simulated agent output
  2. Runs the sanitizer pipeline (keyword pre-filter → regex → entropy check) on each
  3. Reports throughput and latency
- Add an assertion-style test (not just benchmark) that fails if median latency for a 100KB trace exceeds 10ms on a single core
- The 10ms threshold should be configurable via environment variable for CI environments

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `cargo bench --bench sanitize` produces latency measurements
- [ ] A 100KB trace file sanitizes in <10ms median on modern hardware
- [ ] The Aho-Corasick keyword pre-filter demonstrably reduces candidate rules (benchmark shows skip rate)
- [ ] CI runs the assertion-style test (not full criterion benchmark, which is expensive)
